lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 7: Deployments and ReplicaSets
lesson.description: Run Pods through a Deployment: self-healing, scaling, a rolling update with maxSurge and maxUnavailable, a stuck rollout and a rollback, all tested on kind.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Run Pods through a Deployment. Change the Pod template to roll out, watch rollout status, and fix a bad release by applying the last good file.

cheatsheet.intro: How a Deployment rolls, and the commands from Lesson 7.

rows.name: Deployment
rows.role: Keeps the replicas you asked for and rolls them when the Pod template changes.

rows.name: ReplicaSet
rows.role: One per Pod template version. It keeps its own Pods at the count the Deployment gives it.

rows.name: Pod template
rows.role: Only a change here starts a rollout. Changing `replicas` scales, and starts no rollout.

rows.name: selector
rows.role: Must match the template labels. It is immutable after creation.

rows.name: maxSurge / maxUnavailable
rows.role: Both default to 25%. The cheat sheet says not both 0.

rows.name: Recreate
rows.role: Stops the old Pods before starting new ones. Expect a gap in service.

rows.name: progress deadline
rows.role: How long a rollout may stall. The default is 600 seconds.

rows.name: revision history
rows.role: How many old ReplicaSets to keep. The default is 10.

items.what: A Deployment owns one ReplicaSet per Pod template version, and each ReplicaSet keeps its Pods at the requested count.
Only changes to the Pod template start a rollout. `maxSurge` and `maxUnavailable` set its pace.
`kubectl rollout status` tells you when a rollout is done or stuck. A stuck rollout leaves the old Pods serving.
`rollout undo` brings back an old template as a new revision. Then fix the file so `apply` and the cluster agree.

commands.note: the next apply of the file wins

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace `k8s-from-zero`, with the context namespace set as in part 6. The lesson does not print a cluster name. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What does a Deployment own, and what does each of those keep?
exercises.a: A Deployment owns one ReplicaSet per Pod template version, and each ReplicaSet keeps its Pods at the requested count.

exercises.q: Which change starts a rollout, and which change does not?
exercises.a: Only a change to the Pod template starts a rollout. Changing `replicas` scales and starts none.

exercises.q: What do `maxSurge` and `maxUnavailable` default to, and what does `strategy.type: Recreate` do?
exercises.a: Both default to 25%. The cheat sheet says not both 0. `Recreate` stops the old Pods before starting new ones, so expect a gap in service.

exercises.q: Draft a Deployment with the dry-run command in the cheat sheet, apply it, and run `kubectl rollout status deployment/web --timeout=90s`. What exit code means the rollout finished?
exercises.a: Exit 0. The cheat sheet says the command returns when the rollout is complete.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl get deploy,rs,pods`. What do the names share?
exercises.a: The template hash. The cheat sheet says the names share it.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl rollout undo deployment/web`. What does the lesson say this creates?
exercises.a: A new revision. It brings back an old template as that new revision. Then fix the file so apply and the cluster agree.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: Apply fails with `selector` does not match template `labels`. What must be true of the labels?
exercises.a: The labels under `spec.template.metadata.labels` must include everything in `spec.selector.matchLabels`.

exercises.q: Apply fails with `spec.selector: Invalid value: ... field is immutable`. What are the two ways out in the lesson?
exercises.a: Delete and recreate the Deployment, or create a new one under a new name and move traffic. The selector cannot change after creation.

exercises.q: You `kubectl scale`, then the next deploy puts the old count back. Why?
exercises.a: The file still says the old number. Change `replicas` in the file. The next apply of the file wins.

exercises.q: `rollout status` waits forever or reports `exceeded its progress deadline`. What does the lesson tell you to read, and what keeps serving?
exercises.a: Run `kubectl get pods` and `kubectl describe pod` on the newest Pod. A stuck rollout leaves the old Pods serving. Fix the file and apply, or `rollout undo`.
